findings.statement: A compact sum of feedback-sensitive and common noise contributions predicts the reserved injection ratio, but the selected extension loses to the simpler fixed-exponent domain control. This supports bounded reproduction and model ambiguity, not a new laser-noise law.

reliability.rationale: Frozen shared-floor model MAE 3.04916533 dB is worse than fixed domain control 3.01526846 dB and better than flexible 3.165752. One held injection curve supports only bounded reproduction and model ambiguity.

mechanism.rationale: A sum of feedback-sensitive and common spectral noise terms is plausible but two development injection ratios do not identify distinct physical origins or independently establish feedback exponent and floor.

novelty.rationale: Existing source analyses and standard response families are disclosed. This review does not certify exhaustive literature novelty; the result is reproduction.

significance.rationale: Useful transparent spectral-response baseline across an intermediate injection setting, not a new laser-noise relationship.
